candidate_additions: Rdh11 introduced as a novel SREBP2-regulated hepatocyte cholesterol-homeostasis gene (induced by statins, reduced by high-fat/cholesterol diet, co-regulated with Hmgcr/Ldlr) — a gene not mentioned anywhere in the baseline

Erg28 given an explicit functional assignment as the non-catalytic scaffold of the C4-demethylation complex, SREBP2 co-regulated, whose loss impairs SREBP2 activation (baseline only listed Erg28 as a supporting gene without functional detail)
Four distinctive genes (Ddr2, Cetn2, Zfp839, Tas2r138) explicitly flagged as having no retrieved evidence linking them to the pathway
Gene-specific phenotype evidence added: hepatocyte Cyp51 knockout causes liver injury/oval-cell response/fibrosis; Tm7sf2 deficiency causes lipid accumulation and ER stress in regenerating liver
Mechanistic detail that Acss2 acts independently of Acly and that dual Acss2+Acly inhibition is needed to suppress hepatic lipogenesis
Mechanistic detail on Mttp-Acat2 interaction: Mttp relieves product inhibition of Acat2-mediated cholesteryl ester synthesis, linking esterification to VLDL export
Quantitative detail that Scap knockout reduces hepatic cholesterol synthesis by ~80%
MASLD/NASH-specific detail that dysregulated Scap:Insig1 ratios drive free cholesterol accumulation
candidate_removed_or_weakened: Baseline's broader 'aging and MASLD' framing for the Dgat2/Mttp coupling mechanism is narrowed in the candidate to MASLD/NASH context only, dropping the aging reference
decision_relevant_differences: Rdh11 as a newly asserted SREBP2 target gene could prompt follow-up validation or inclusion in the gene program that baseline did not suggest
Erg28's clarified mechanistic role (scaffold vs. undefined supporting gene) changes how a reader would prioritize it for functional follow-up
Explicit non-evidence flag for Ddr2/Cetn2/Zfp839/Tas2r138 helps a reader triage which distinctive genes still need investigation, which baseline left implicit
assessment.rationale: Both annotations converge on the same central biological story: P21 is the hepatic de novo cholesterol biosynthesis pathway under SCAP/INSIG1-SREBP2 transcriptional control, balanced against Ldlr-mediated uptake, fed by Acss2-derived acetyl-CoA, and coupled to Dgat2/Mttp-driven VLDL-TG export in the MASLD context. No mechanism, direction, or regulatory relationship is reversed or contradicted. The candidate's value-add is (1) a new gene-function claim (Rdh11 as an SREBP2 target), (2) a specific mechanistic role for Erg28 that was previously just a listed gene, (3) explicit acknowledgment of unexplained distinctive genes, and (4) denser gene-specific and context-specific literature support (KO phenotypes, Acss2/Acly relationship, Mttp-Acat2 interaction, quantitative Scap effect size). These are meaningful refinements and gene-function assignments layered onto an unchanged core interpretation, not a change in the program's biological identity or the direction of any regulatory effect.
shared_core_conclusions: P21 is the near-complete mevalonate-pathway/post-squalene de novo cholesterol biosynthesis program in mouse hepatocytes (Hmgcs1 through Dhcr7, plus Acat2 esterification)
Program transcription is gated by the SCAP/INSIG1-SREBP2 sterol-sensing feedback circuit: Scap knockout abrogates the program, Insig1 knockout hyperactivates it
Ldlr knockout drives compensatory upregulation of de novo synthesis, forming the uptake/synthesis balance limb
Acss2 supplies acetyl-CoA substrate for the pathway
Dgat2 and Mttp couple cholesterol synthesis to VLDL-triglyceride assembly/export, relevant to hepatic lipid handling in MASLD
